description:
This two-line program never finishes compiling on interp (killed at 15-30 s; the full distiller ran 36 min at 100% CPU, 1.7 GB), on every snapshot that has Stream.map/2, including d9c9a842c from before fz-sc8.99:

  Enum.to_list(Stream.map([1], &(&1)))
  Enum.to_list(Map.put(%{}, 1, 1))

Elixir runs it. Each line alone compiles in 0.1 s, and so does the pair with a literal map (%{1 => 2}). It takes an Enum call over a Stream.map plus an Enum call over a map built at run time (Map.put, Map.new) that goes through Enumerable.Map.reduce; Enum.sum(Map.values(m)) and map_size(m) do not trigger it. Enum.count, Enum.sum and Enum.to_list all do.

Telemetry (activation_analysis.defined per function, 44174db13) at 10 s / 30 s: Stream.compose/2#lambda@0/2 365/500, Enumerable.Stream.reduce/3 143/197, List.reduce_cont/3 116/159, Enumerable.List.reduce/3 98/138, Map.reduce_cont/5 86/128, Range.reduce_cont/6 78/122 (Range is never used), Map.reduce/3 89/121; 1739/2389 activations total. Throughput falls: 14.5k records in 10 s, 18.9k in 30 s. Activations keep being minted: a key dimension is not bounded.

The repro is the fixture; acceptance includes a minimal predicted job trace. Blocks fz-sc8.19: the distiller hits it as soon as it resolves (after Map.update/4).

## Design (page ../fz-sc8.117.html, approved 2026-11-11)
Cause: Map.put returns any, so Enumerable dispatch on it reaches every impl incl. Stream; Stream's enum field is any, so Stream.reduce re-dispatches and reaches Stream again with reducer L(R) -> L(L(R)) ...; every depth is a new key; no bound applies to a Whole callable slot (ADDRESS_COLLAPSE_DEPTH is list-only, erase_closure_identity keeps captures at every depth).
Fix: a fourth termination fact. No activation key holds a closure of a lambda inside the captures of a closure of the same lambda; the inner one becomes `fun`, the callable top (the lattice has no arity-n callable class: an all-`any` arrow is equivalent to `fun` but interns as a second id and minted duplicate keys, and an arrow with variables makes resolve_closure_call wait forever). One memoized idempotent Types::fold_self_nested_closures, applied in derive_activation_key_arrow on every slot (Whole included) before brand erasure. Values keep exact types; only keys fold. Nesting is then bounded by the program's lambda count.
Measured (c768670cd, e1.fz): the fold ends the ladder; 209 activations total, compiles in ~1.1 s (baseline still growing at 1030 keys when killed at 10 s). The prediction (impl reduce <= 3, compose lambda <= 2) was not met: compose lambda 42, Enumerable.List.reduce 6, Stream.reduce 5, Map.reduce 4, Range.reduce 4. Closure nesting is gone; the remainder is the entry axis (any, {any, any}, int | float, int) times the acc axis (list, any, empty_list(), list({any, any}), list(int)), which is fz-sc8.127 / fz-y5x territory. A drive_test pins the counts and asserts no key self-nests; fixture 01068 checks the output against elixir. No 00773 pin moved. Closures only; the tuple ladder (fixtures2/behavior/return_tuple_accumulator.fz, deferred) is the same failure and this fact is its template. Docs: type-specialization.md termination section gains the fact; stale erase_transported_closure_identities names updated.
title: An Enum call over a Stream next to one over a built map finishes compiling
